// Tools owns every tool handler. A pointer receiver is used so the MCP
// server can keep a single handle and call methods by name via AddTool.
type Tools struct {
	Metrics *observability.Metrics
	Tracer  observability.Tracer
	Backend *Backend
}

// GetRfc implements the "get_rfc" tool. Handler shape
// mirrors docs/guide/mcp-server-in-go.md §11 — span, subject attribution,
// input parse, backend call, outcome metric, structured log.
func (t *Tools) GetRfc(ctx context.Context, req mcp.CallToolRequest) (*mcp.CallToolResult, error) {
	start := time.Now()
	subj, _ := mcpauth.SubjectFromContext(ctx)

	ctx, span := t.Tracer.Start(ctx, "mcp.tool.get_rfc")
	defer span.End()
	span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("mcp.subject", subj.Name))

	id, err := req.RequireString("id")
	if err != nil {
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "bad_input", start)
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(err.Error()), nil
	}
	_ = id

	rawPath := strings.NewReplacer(
		"{id}", url.PathEscape(id),
	).Replace("/rfcs/{id}")

	u, err := url.Parse(t.Backend.BaseURL + rawPath)
	if err != nil {
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "bad_input", start)
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(fmt.Sprintf("build url: %v", err)), nil
	}

	httpReq, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, http.MethodGet, u.String(), nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "network_error", start)
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(fmt.Sprintf("build request: %v", err)), nil
	}

	if t.Backend.Token != "" {
		httpReq.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+t.Backend.Token)
	}

	resp, err := t.Backend.Client.Do(httpReq)
	if err != nil {
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "network_error", start)
		slog.WarnContext(ctx, "mcp tool upstream call failed",
			"tool", "get_rfc",
			"mcp.subject", subj.Name,
			"outcome", "network_error",
			"duration_ms", time.Since(start).Milliseconds(),
			"err", err.Error())
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(fmt.Sprintf("upstream request failed: %v", err)), nil
	}
	defer func() { _ = resp.Body.Close() }()

	body, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, 1<<20))
	if err != nil {
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "network_error", start)
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(fmt.Sprintf("read response: %v", err)), nil
	}

	switch {
	case resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300:
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "success", start)
		slog.InfoContext(ctx, "mcp tool completed",
			"tool", "get_rfc",
			"mcp.subject", subj.Name,
			"outcome", "success",
			"duration_ms", time.Since(start).Milliseconds())
		return mcp.NewToolResultText(string(body)), nil
	case resp.StatusCode >= 400 && resp.StatusCode < 500:
		t.recordOutcome("get_rfc", subj.Name, "upstream_4xx", start)
		return mcp.NewToolResultError(fmt.Sprintf("upstream %d: %s", resp.StatusCode, string(body))), nil

// recordOutcome increments the two tool-level counters for every
// terminated handler. Called from every exit path so metrics are
// complete even when the handler returns an error result.
func (t *Tools) recordOutcome(tool, subject, outcome string, start time.Time) {
	t.Metrics.ToolInvocations.WithLabelValues(tool, subject, outcome).Inc()
	t.Metrics.ToolDuration.WithLabelValues(tool, outcome).Observe(time.Since(start).Seconds())
}
